response.query: What criteria justify adding a comparator school versus defending a single-case critical/typical-case logic in language policy studies?
response.answer: Adding a comparator school provides broader context and enhances validity in language policy studies; defending a single-case logic may lack generalizability and comparative insights.

results.title: America's Censored Classrooms 2024
results.content: Finally, this past year also saw the introduction of 29 bills with higher education provisions that, while not constituting direct censorship of educational speech the way gag orders do, would have eroded institutions and practices that make academic freedom in colleges and universities possible. This law authorizes public college and university boards of trustees to deny or revoke tenure if a faculty member is “unlikely to foster a culture of free inquiry, free expression, and intellectual diversity within the institution,”; is “unlikely to expose students to scholarly works from a variety of political or ideological frameworks that may exist within and are applicable to the faculty member’s academic discipline”; or is “likely, while performing teaching duties within the scope of the faculty member’s employment, to subject students to political or ideological views and opinions that are unrelated to the faculty member’s academic discipline or assigned course of instruction.” In addition to denial or loss of tenure, the faculty member can be terminated or demoted, have their salary reduced, or face some other disciplinary action.
